dialog.body: Utilities, water and sewer billing, this is Tony. How can I help you this morning?
Good morning, Tony, thank you for taking my call. My name is Timothy Peckham. I'm on speakerphone, I hope that's all right, thank you. And please feel free to interrupt me if I go on too long.
No problem at all, speakerphone's fine. What's going on with the account?

Well, thank you. I just bought a house, at 309 Bacheller Street, in the Fifth Ward. We closed about two weeks ago. And the first water and sewer bill came in the mail, and it's made out to the former owner. Not to me. Thank you.
Okay, yeah, that happens a lot with a new sale. The bill follows the property, but the name on the account doesn't always get switched right away. Do you have the bill in front of you?

I do, I have it right here. Thank you. The bill date at the top says November twenty-fourth. And the due date is, um, December twenty-fourth. So that's, I mean, it's wrong, it's not even my name on it, and I'd like it fixed, please.
Sure. Can you read me the name that's on it and the account number, just so I find the right one?
Certainly. The name is Harlan Voss, V-O-S-S. And the account number, give me a second, thank you, is the one in the top right corner. It's, um, [pause] 4, 4, 1, 0, 7, 2.

Got it, 441072. Okay, I see it. So here's what's happening. That bill covers a reading period that was mostly before you closed. The meter reading was taken the middle of November, so the usage on it is the old owner's. Your first bill in your own name will come after the next reading.
I see. Thank you. But then why was it mailed to me, if it's not my usage? That seems, with respect, a little sloppy. Thank you.

Fair point. It went to the property address because nobody had updated the mailing address yet. If your closing attorney's office sent over the sale paperwork, we'll have the transfer on file, and I can check if that came through.
I believe it was sent. Thank you. I'd just like to be sure it's not going to be sent to collections or anything with the wrong person's name on it. Thank you.
No, nothing like that. I'll put a note on the account that the property changed hands, and I'll switch the billing name to yours going forward. Can I get your name spelled?
Of course. Timothy, T-I-M-O-T-H-Y. Peckham, P-E-C-K-H-A-M. Thank you.

Peckham, got it. Now the final bill for Mr. Voss, that's between him and the closing, usually the sellers settle up the water at the table. If it's still open, it may get adjusted. I'd say hold on to that paper bill in case your closing paperwork shows a water adjustment.

Understood, thank you. Now, the other thing, and you can interrupt me, I'm leaving on a trip this weekend. I'll be gone for about three weeks, thank you. If I do owe something on this bill, how do I pay it before I go? Without coming into City Hall, I mean, because I won't have time. Is there a way outside regular hours?

Yeah, a few ways. You can pay online through the city's website with a card, any time of day. There's also a payment drop box outside City Hall for checks, that's available around the clock. And you can mail a check with the stub from the bill.
The drop box, thank you. Is that, um, easy to find? I haven't been to City Hall in a while, thank you.

It's by the entrance, you can't miss it. Just put the check and the stub in an envelope with the account number on the check memo line. But honestly, with the name issue, let me first look at what's actually owed on this one.
Yes, please, thank you. I'd rather not pay it if it isn't mine.

Okay, one sec. [pause] Alright, so the balance on it is for that reading period, and it's not been paid yet. Whether it's yours or not depends on what your closing did. I'd call your closing office and ask if water was prorated. If it was, you don't owe this. If not, you'd pay it, and then you've got the paper trail.
That's helpful. Thank you. I'll call them this afternoon. And if I can't get an answer before I leave, I'd just pay it by the drop box, then sort it out later. Is that sensible? Thank you.
That's sensible. Pay it, keep your closing papers, and if it turns out the seller covered it, you'd have a credit on the account for next time.
Wonderful. Thank you. And the due date again is December twenty-fourth, correct? I want to be certain, thank you.

That's what's on the bill, yep. You'll be back before then probably, but doing it before you leave is the safe move. Also, the weather's going to be rough today with the nor'easter, so I wouldn't go out to the drop box this afternoon if you can help it.
Good point, thank you. I'll wait until the storm passes tomorrow. I appreciate your time, Tony, thank you very much.
Anytime, Mr. Peckham. I've got the name change noted. Safe travels, and stay dry today.
Thank you, you too. Goodbye.
